definitions.gloss: part-time school system; evening school; fixed-schedule schooling
definitions.explanation: A schooling system, especially at the high school level, where classes are held at set times outside regular daytime hours — typically in the evening. Designed for students who work during the day.

examples.japanese: {定時制|ていじせい}⟦{高校|こうこう}→高校：01083_koukou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{通|かよ}っている→通う：01217_kayou⟧。
examples.english: I attend a part-time high school.

examples.english: I graduated from evening school while working.

examples.english: The part-time course typically takes four years to complete, but some schools allow graduation in three.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{定時|ていじ}→定時：07697_teiji⟧ (fixed time, scheduled time) and ⟦{制|せい}→〜制：30791_sei⟧ (system). Refers primarily to {定時制|ていじせい}⟦{高校|こうこう}→高校：01083_koukou⟧ — high schools that hold classes in the evening (or sometimes morning/afternoon) for students who cannot attend regular full-time school.

CULTURAL NOTE:
{定時制|ていじせい}⟦{高校|こうこう}→高校：01083_koukou⟧ was originally established after World War II for working youth who needed to earn a living while completing their education. Today's students come from diverse backgrounds — working adults, students who left full-time school, and older learners. The standard course is four years rather than the usual three.

- {定時制|ていじせい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{通|かよ}う→通う：01217_kayou⟧ — to attend part-time school
